title: Match code trust to the runner boundary
description: Choose a workload and an execution pool. The model checks runner eligibility and names the concrete exposure created by persistence, host access, tags, protected refs, and credentials.

scenarios.label: Fork merge request
scenarios.detail: Repository-controlled code from an untrusted contributor needs build capacity but no protected credential.

scenarios.label: Default-branch build
scenarios.detail: Reviewed code produces a release candidate but does not need authority over production.

scenarios.label: Production deployment
scenarios.detail: A protected-ref job needs a short-lived deployment identity and an isolated production capability.

pools.label: Persistent shell runner
pools.detail: A long-lived host accepts general build jobs and executes them as the runner service account.
pools.credentialDetail: No production identity is configured, but jobs share a persistent host boundary.

pools.label: Ephemeral build pool
pools.detail: Each general build job receives a fresh, unprivileged execution environment without deployment authority.
pools.credentialDetail: The pool carries no production credential.

pools.label: Protected deployment pool
pools.detail: A separate ephemeral pool accepts only protected-ref jobs with the production deployment tag.
pools.credentialDetail: The job requests a short-lived identity token for the deployment broker.
